intro: Each simulated device connects to the gateway just like a real GPS and travels a route. Before starting it, add it to an account with “Add GPS”, with the same identifier and the same brand.

tabs.label: What to see of the simulator

list.title: Simulated devices
list.empty: There are none yet. Create the first one to see a vehicle move without a GPS connected.

problem.rejected: The gateway rejected it: is it added to the platform with this identifier and this brand?
problem.silent: The device is sending, but the platform receives nothing: is it added to the platform with this identifier and this brand?
problem.unreachable: Could not connect to {{host}}, port {{port}}. Check the server and the port.
problem.unregistered: This identifier is not added to the platform yet. Add it with “Add GPS” or the gateway will reject it.
problem.noSignal_one: It has no signal at this point of its route: it keeps {{count}} report and uploads it when the signal is back.
problem.noSignal_other: It has no signal at this point of its route: it keeps {{count}} reports and uploads them when the signal is back.

form.name: Name
form.hintImei: A 15-digit IMEI. Use the same one when adding the GPS to the platform.
form.hintDigits: An ID of {{length}} digits. Use the same one when adding the GPS to the platform.
form.connectionNote: As on a real GPS: the server and the port it reports to. They start as this platform's public address and the brand's port; change them to send somewhere else.
form.end: At the end of the route
form.rest: Seconds switched off at the end
form.restHint: With 180 or more, each lap is recorded as a trip with its stop.
form.restartNote: It is running: on saving, it starts its trip over with what you change.
form.timedHint: This route brings the time of each street: the speed only counts where it brings none.

routes.title: Routes
routes.empty: There are no routes. Create the first one so a simulated device has somewhere to go.
routes.removeText: The route “{{name}}” is deleted. Simulated devices and their history are not touched.
routes.editorNote: Mark where it goes: search for an address or tap the map.
routes.mapHint: Tap the map to add a point. Drag a point to move it.
routes.name: Name
routes.pointsNeeded: Mark at least two points: where it starts and where it ends
routes.tooManyPoints: A route takes up to {{max}} points

modeNote.streets: The path follows the streets between the points and the vehicle goes at the speed of each one.
modeNote.streetsOff: The routing service is off: turn it on in Settings or use straight lines.
modeNote.straight: A straight line from each point to the next, at the speed the simulated device has.
modeNote.kept: The path is kept as it came. Choose “Along streets” or “Straight lines” to trace it again between its points.

routes.searchPlaceholder: Search for an address or a place
routes.searchEmpty: That place was not found. Write it another way or mark the point on the map.
routes.summaryEmpty: Mark where it starts and where it ends.
routes.summaryUntraced: Press “Trace route” to see the path along streets.
routes.summaryStale: The points changed: trace the route again.
routes.inUseNote_one: A simulated device travels this route: on saving it starts over on the changed path.
routes.inUseNote_other: {{count}} simulated devices travel this route: on saving they start over on the changed path.

options.title: Route options
options.note: What happens to the vehicle on the way out, to test how the platform responds.
options.presetNote: It replaces what is in the list. What this brand does not carry is left out.

presets.theft: Theft: power cut, tow and jammer

options.empty: Nothing yet: the vehicle just travels its route.
options.fuelNote: For the platform to read it, set up the vehicle's tank with the “io89” value as a percentage.
options.driverNote: 4 to 16 hexadecimal digits, the same the driver has in the platform.
options.reportIgnition: It does not say whether the engine is on: it only gives the voltage
options.roadSpeeds: It follows the speed of each street
options.extraIoHint: Number=value, separated by commas. For example, 66=11500 reports 11.5 V of vehicle battery.

problem.km: The kilometer must be within the route
problem.percent: The points of the tank go from 1 to 100
problem.stretch: The stretch is at least 50 meters long
problem.speed: The speed goes from 5 to 250 km/h
problem.driver: The driver key has 4 to 16 hexadecimal digits (0-9, A-F)
problem.codes: Each fault code is a letter (P, C, B or U) and four digits, such as P0300; up to 8
problem.fuel: The level goes from 0 to 100 and the burn from 0 to 100 points every 100 km
problem.extraIo: Extra parameters are written as number=value, separated by commas

live.notExpected: Does not apply: it sends to another server
live.logEmpty: Nothing yet. Once started, its connection and every command it receives show up here.

control.title: Live control
control.note: What you do here happens to the device right now, to see how the platform responds.
control.stopped: Start it to trigger alarms and events live.
control.theftNote: A power cut and 5 minutes of movement with the engine off, with a jammer.
control.fuelNote: It stops with the engine off while the level changes.
control.disconnectNote: It stops transmitting, keeps its reports and uploads them when it is back.
control.backfill: Send the route as a past trip
control.backfillNote: A whole lap of its route, as if it had traveled it before: it is in the history without waiting.
control.backfillDone_one: {{count}} report was sent. The trip is already in that day's history.
control.backfillDone_other: {{count}} reports were sent. The trip is already in that day's history.
control.range: Seconds go from 1 to 86400, points from 1 to 100 and hours from 0 to 720

log.resumed: Resumed when the server restarted, towards {{host}}, port {{port}}
log.rejected: The gateway rejected it: is it added to the platform with this identifier?
log.unreachable: Could not connect to {{host}}, port {{port}} ({{reason}}); it keeps trying
log.closed: The gateway closed the connection; it connects again
log.engineCut: Engine start cut: the vehicle stops
log.engineResume: Engine start given back: the vehicle goes on with its route
log.signalLost: Lost its signal: it keeps what it cannot send
log.signalBack: The signal is back: it uploaded {{count}} stored reports
log.theft: Theft mode: a power cut and {{seconds}} s of movement with the engine off
log.fuelChange: Fuel: {{pct}} points in {{seconds}} s, stopped with the engine off
log.backfill: Uploaded its route as a past trip: {{count}} reports, ended {{hours}} h ago

remove.title: Delete simulated device
remove.text: “{{name}}” is deleted from the simulator. The vehicle and its history on the platform are not touched.
